neighboring_unit_entries.title: Finite difference, its kernel, and a decay-qualified inverse
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Writing the proposed Hamiltonian as a similarity transform through Delta exposes the key structural issue: Delta is a unit shift difference, annihilates unit-periodic functions, and therefore has no inverse on all smooth functions. The authors restrict attention to functions vanishing at infinity and give a Bernoulli/Borel prescription whose right-inverse property is tied to that boundary choice.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is done by conjugating a dilation-type operator with a finite-difference operator and then using a boundary value at the origin to turn its spectral parameter into a zeta zero. The remaining claims are a conditional program for reality, an inner product, and degeneracy, not a completed spectral realization.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source proposes a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian formed by placing the symmetrized dilation operator between a unit-shift difference and its formal inverse. Requiring every eigenfunction to vanish at the origin is said to make one half of one minus i times each eigenvalue a nontrivial zero of ζ; the overview also states a 2xp commuting limit, modified PT symmetry, a new pairing, and a degeneracy consequence for off-critical zeros.
directed.conceptual_reading: Similarity transport is used to recode analytic zero data as boundary-selected spectral data. The key compression is that one boundary condition is intended to perform both zero selection and later operator-theoretic work.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the finite-difference operator, the symmetrized dilation Hamiltonian, the spectral parameter z, and the origin evaluation of the eventual Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunction.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Every headline conclusion remains formal or conditional here. In particular, the span does not establish a self-adjoint domain, spectral completeness, or reality of the proposed eigenvalues, so it is not an RH proof.

section_entries.mathematical_role: Uses a distributional pairing to distinguish nontrivial from trivial states, relates the origin boundary condition to momentum symmetry, states exceptional-point consequences, notes infinite norms and a cutoff regularization, and isolates domain/completeness as open.

unit_result_entry.title: Off-critical zeros are represented as exceptional-point degeneracies
unit_result_entry.why_material: The source claims that if RH is false, eigenstates associated with off-critical nontrivial zeros coalesce into Jordan-block structures and satisfy self-orthogonality. It then connects spectral nondegeneracy to simplicity of zeros, but explicitly makes the strongest simplicity conclusion depend on a one-to-one correspondence between eigenstate boundary conditions and the secular equation.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The exceptional-point and simplicity statements are consequences within the formal spectral model. The one-to-one correspondence needed for the all-roots simplicity conclusion is posed conditionally, not proved here.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The origin boundary condition is reused to suppress integration-by-parts terms
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Because the metric commutes with momentum, the source reduces momentum symmetry to vanishing boundary terms in paired original and adjoint states. The adjoint state diverges at the origin, so sufficient vanishing of the original state is needed; the already imposed condition at zero is said to suffice. Under that assumption, a formal integral rearrangement makes H symmetric in the new inner product.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Infinite norms motivate a finite-window regularization
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source separates its formal Hamiltonian analysis from ordinary quantum mechanics because the states are not normalizable, then proposes a symmetric multiplicative cutoff, logarithmic state renormalization, and a limit. It reports that the transformed-position expectation has the same leading scale as prime counting.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The formal model recodes an off-critical zero as an exceptional point: paired spectral data coalesce into a Jordan structure and the eigenstate becomes self-orthogonal. This turns failure of the critical-line condition into a specific non-diagonalizable spectral pathology rather than merely a nonreal eigenvalue.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source states that RH would make the proposed eigenvalues nondegenerate, whereas an off-critical nontrivial zero would produce coalescing eigenstates, a Jordan block, and self-orthogonality at a complex exceptional point. It then discusses simplicity of zeta zeros: the strongest conclusion that RH implies all zeros simple is explicitly conditioned on a one-to-one correspondence between eigenfunction boundary conditions and the secular equation.
directed.conceptual_reading: Degeneracy and self-orthogonality are used as obstruction signatures. The representation aims to distinguish critical-line zeros through diagonalizable spectral behavior and off-critical zeros through exceptional-point behavior.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Functional pairing of zeta zeros, the eigenvalue parametrization, biorthogonal self-pairing, and Jordan blocks bridge analytic zero location to non-Hermitian degeneracy.
directed.boundary_or_failure: These are consequences inside the formal spectral model, not independent evidence for RH. The required one-to-one boundary/secular correspondence and a valid operator domain are not proved, so the global simplicity claim remains conditional.
directed.uncertainty: The prose claims are legible; exact self-orthogonality notation and critical-line fractions remain extraction-sensitive.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive unresolved object is not another formal eigenfunction but the operator domain. In infinite dimensions, biorthogonality does not identify the true adjoint without completeness, so the formal chain from boundary condition to momentum symmetry to pseudo-Hermiticity cannot yet be closed.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The discussion calls identification of the Hamiltonian domain and establishment of self-adjointness difficult open problems. Revisiting the boundary condition, it contrasts finite-dimensional nondegenerate matrices, where biorthogonality can identify the adjoint, with the infinite-dimensional setting, where completeness of the proposed eigenstates is additionally required. The observed pairing is said only to suggest the momentum-Hermiticity assumption.
directed.conceptual_reading: Completeness is the missing bridge between formal eigenvector algebra and operator theory. Without it, a candidate dual basis and vanishing boundary terms do not determine the adjoint or certify spectral reality.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge that remains to be built consists of a precise domain, a complete eigenstate system, control of the adjoint, and a self-adjoint or otherwise adequate closed realization.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This limitation blocks upgrading the pseudo-Hermitian and biorthogonal calculations to a rigorous RH implication. Formal symmetry, self-adjointness, completeness, and spectral reality must remain distinct.
directed.uncertainty: The central caveat is prose-level and not dependent on damaged formulas; uncertainty concerns the unresolved mathematics itself rather than extraction.
